title: Answers to Six Questions Concerning Ideal Topological Groups
content: We answer six questions concerning ideal topological groups posed by Jafari and Rajesh in Questions and Answers in General Topology 44 (2026), 17–19. The questions concern minimality, sequential com-pleteness, precompactness, τ-precompactness, separately I-continuous multiplication, and jointly ideal-continuous multiplication. The first two questions require care because the generalized notion of I-continuity is weaker than ordinary continuity and therefore classical compactness arguments cannot simply be transferred without additional hypotheses. We formulate sufficient ideal-compactness conditions under which the desired conclusions follow. For Questions 3–6 we give explicit construc-tions. In particular, compact groups equipped with the ideal of finite subsets provide τ-precompact examples for every infinite cardinal τ. Furthermore, the finite group Z3 with the non-discrete topology τ = ∅, 1, 2, Z3 and ideal I = ∅, 0 provides a genuinely non-classical example: it is an ideal topological group although it is not an ordinary topological group. Consequently it supplies explicit examples for both separately ideal-continuous semitopological groups and jointly ideal-continuous paratopological groups.
